rationale: Three observed points (attempt-00: 147.72us; attempt-01: 147.67us; attempt-02: 147.67us) are nearly identical in simulated latency and share exactly 33.816576 MB simulated DRAM regardless of swizzle (0/8/16) and block_K (32/64). Since reuse is capped at ceil(M/block_M)=1 for block_M=32, the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis has no structural leverage here; swizzle cannot reduce A reloads. I therefore downweight traffic to 0.5 (it is dominated by the fixed B read and observed DRAM is invariant) and downweight footprint to 0.5 since smem has not been a binding differentiator (18KB vs 24KB both fine under the 32768 cap). block_M is pinned at 32 (M=32 must be divided exactly; 64/128 cannot tile it). block_N stays {64,128} to test whether widened N tiles reduce block count/latency; block_K {32,64} and stages {2,3} retained because stages=3 with block_K=32 already produced the best latency. Pipeline weight raised to 2 to favor deeper overlap/less K-per-stage serialization, which is the main lever observed to have any (small) effect. Launches stays 0.5 since ceil(M/32)=1 makes it nearly constant across tuples. Shared cap kept at 32768 (hard portability cap dominates the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N)). Next hypothesis: block_N=128 or stage-3/K-64 variants may shave the small latency gap; if DRAM and latency remain flat across new tuples, further downweight traffic/footprint and treat this shape as bandwidth-flat. Scope: simulated_us and simulated_dram_mb are GB10 simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. Local revision from three observed points, not a global optimality claim.
